original_card.question: Can a new local cost interface change the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio beyond current packing?
methods: Propose a changed helper inventory and derive an optimistic exact moment.
Design a small completed instance and independently verify its endpoint and rank bill.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A new physically realizable contract outside the frozen catalogue whose per-call profile, screened with ceiling.ceiling(), beats the selected word's packing ceiling; a lower cap does not establish identical circuitry or order attainable optima, and is insufficient to pass the stronger-budget target under this model. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Packing of the selected word is capped at +0.87% (ceiling model); only a lower local excess spend or a changed coverage law raises the cap.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one changed boundary or helper type with explicit counts.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Mixing only providers already inside the pinned catalogue.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: Can a new local cost interface change the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio beyond current packing?
bottleneck_link: The deficit side of the ratio is closed exactly: under the unchanged coverage interface the per-call deficit unpaid*w - centre = 320/9 does not depend on the helper inventory at all, so any new local cost interface moves the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio only through the recursive-cost side. This package measures that movement for the two recorded changed-helper-inventory contracts outside the frozen catalogue (R489, R480): both move it the wrong way, their optimistic exact moments sitting strictly below the selected word's packing ceiling by 0.406% and 0.0168% relative. The only screened direction that moves it favorably is the same-inventory PR987 U10 profile family, at most +0.082% at its nonnegativity boundary, two orders of magnitude below the target scale and inside the +0.87% packing headroom the bottleneck records.
stop_rule: Screen the two recorded new-inventory contracts (R489 from PR1004, R480 from PR1005) and one bounded mass-neutral direction family of 22 profiles with the exact packing ceiling at grid 1e-12; stop at the strict-bracket verdict. Kill the recorded new-inventory route early when neither contract beats the selected ceiling; allow one bounded pivot to the direction family; run no synthesis or construction round without a passing screen.
evidence: research/helper-inventory-moment-seede64193c0/RESULT.json (byte-stable receipt: exact ceiling brackets at grid 1e-12 for the selected word, R489, R480 and all 22 family profiles; deficit 320/9 and rank bill 7232 per call for every row); verify.py replay PASS_HELPER_INVENTORY_MOMENT_SCREEN with a git-blob cross-check of both SPEC vectors, an independent float endpoint/root cross-check and four rejection controls.

open_questions.question: Can any physically realizable scalar word realize a mass-neutral U10-family profile direction (rank-4 mass split toward ranks 3 and 5) at the selected template, and does its fully charged bill survive?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the only screened direction in this package that strictly beats the selected packing ceiling (up to +0.082% at t = 17), and no word realizing any t has been built; the screen is an optimistic relaxation only.
open_questions.first_step: Pin the t = 1 profile (selected plus four rank-3, minus eight rank-4, plus four rank-5 children per call), attempt one scalar-word construction with the fixed entrances and cleanup contract, and screen its complete charged bill with ceiling.ceiling().
open_questions.blocked_by: No priced changed-word contract exists; any construction round first needs the family-level budget and obligation gate in docs/research/research-family-status.md.

open_questions.question: Do any other recorded changed-helper-inventory contracts outside the 25-interface frozen catalogue beat the selected packing ceiling?
open_questions.why_it_matters: R489 and R480 both fail the screen, but the heterogeneous-owner catalogue bound explicitly leaves the whole new-inventory class open (their reduced costs are negative), so the class is not exhausted by two members.
open_questions.first_step: Collect each outside-catalogue helper width inventory with byte-pinned SPEC vectors and run the same ceiling.ceiling() screen with strict bracket separation.
open_questions.blocked_by: Each contract's per-call profile and helper inventory must be extracted from pinned source blobs; empty coverage is unknown, not evidence of absence.
